items.headline: $28.6M school/daycare project permitted on Rincon Avenue
items.summary: A Phase I new construction permit valued at $28,624,281 was issued for 4333 Rincon Avenue, filed under the city’s school/daycare use type. It is the largest of San José’s notable permits this week.

items.headline: Supermicro permitted for $5.5M server room buildout
items.summary: A tenant improvement permit was issued for Supermicro server rooms at 988 Rock Avenue, valued at $5.5 million, pointing to expanded data-center-style space for the tech manufacturer.

items.headline: Zoning tweak would allow housing in ROLM(E) district
items.summary: The Economic Development Committee is recommending that the City Council amend the zoning code to explicitly allow multi-family residential uses as a conditional use in the ROLM(E) (Research/Office/Light Manufacturing) zone district.

items.headline: Council to hear appeal of Civic Center Drive townhome project
items.summary: The council is scheduled to consider an appeal of a permit approval for a project at 860 and 858 Civic Center Drive and 1526 Alviso Street that would demolish existing buildings and build 14 townhomes plus a duplex with commercial space.

items.headline: Public meeting on environmental review for Oakmead Pkwy housing project
items.summary: A public scoping meeting was held to gather input on the environmental impact report for a proposed residential project at 1250 Oakmead Parkway

items.headline: Council to respond to grand jury report on pothole claims
items.summary: The City Council is set to approve a response to a Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on improving how pothole damage claims are processed.

items.headline: Stanford to keep paying for stadium traffic control
items.summary: The Council is considering a five-year agreement with Stanford University under which the university pays for traffic control services during Stanford Stadium events.
